newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX jumps over one percent on bourse.
newsitem.headline: German DAX jumps over one percent on bourse.

text.p: Germany's 30-share DAX index jumped over one percent in bourse trade, buoyed by the U.S, Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged.
Dealers said the market's mood was positive and that the gains looked likely to hold through the session. Firmer German bonds and a stable dollar gave support to the market.
The 30-share DAX index was trading up 38.91 at 3,582.34 points after about one hour of floor trading.
Degussa and Veba were the focus of attention, after Veba announced that it had taken a 36.4 percent stake in Degussa. Veba gained 1.35 marks to 100.15 while Degussa jumped eight marks to 84 marks.
Analysts predicted further gains in Veba shares.
Thomas Deser of BHF Bank raised Veba to a buy from hold and raised its earnings per share forecast by 10 pfennigs over each of the next two years to 5.70 marks in 1997 and 6.30 marks in 1998.
"This is certainly positive for Veba. It shows Veba as a group moving into a new phase of its activities and it has made clear that this should have a positive effect on earnings," Deser said.

Christine Dienhart, chemicals analyst at Bayerische Vereinsbank in Munich, added: "This is very positive news. The best part is the 86.80 marks per share price paid, which confirms that our own long-term target for the share of 92.50 marks is in the right area."
